description:
The Rule of Flame | Engineering Intelligence for Safer Space Exploration

A one-person team from Sofia, Bulgaria, combining engineering physics, AI and cyber defense. Challenge: Flame in Freefall. Mission: turn NASA's microgravity combustion research into insights that are traceable to their source, checked against the data and clear about their limits. Values: scientific accuracy, honest uncertainty, original work, open code.
summary:
Zero-G Firewall turns NASA’s microgravity combustion research into an interactive, verifiable tool for fire safety in future habitats.

When a smoke alarm goes off in a spacecraft, the first step is to stop the ventilation. In one NASA test that put a flame out in two seconds, yet NASA’s own guide lists the rule as a misconception, and no test exists in lunar gravity. Zero-G Firewall lets anyone see what the evidence supports and where it stops.

It summarises and ranks 24 NASA PSI investigations (2,009 test rows), maps every test by oxygen, pressure and gravity in 3-D, compares a habitat question with recorded tests, and runs a model trained on NASA droplet data that abstains outside its data. A Fire Lab shows smoke transport in a model cabin, and Alarm Trust rejects tampered sensor readings in synthetic attacks. Every number opens a receipt to its NASA file: 4,959 files in a hash chain the browser re-checks.
